previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with idiopathic chronic pancreatitis was admitted for an acute flare characterized by severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, and vomiting. She had been on home TPN due to inability to tolerate oral intake. Initial labs showed normal lipase and LFTs, and a CT scan revealed no acute findings. She was managed with bowel rest, IV fluids, TPN, and IV pain and nausea control. An endoscopy was performed to rule out gastritis or ulcers, which showed normal findings. Her pain and nausea gradually improved, allowing transition to oral medications and advancement to a soft diet. Platelet count, which had been low, normalized by discharge. She was discharged home with continued TPN, oral pain and nausea medications, new constipation regimen, and follow-up plans with gastroenterology and her therapist.

Brief Hospital Course:
Patient is a ___ female with history of chronic idiopathic 
pancreatitis, GERD, seasonal allergies, depression who presented 
with abdominal pain, nausea, reports of vomiting. Her 
presentation was consistent with previous episodes of chronic 
pancreatitis. 
.
# Abdominal pain- Patient's symptoms are consistent with prior 
pancreatitis flares. She has had multiple admissions this year 
for similar flares and has recently had MRCP which showed 
findings c/w chronic pancreatitis with normal secretin test and 
a negative EGD on her last admission here. Her LFTs/lipase/WBC 
are within normal limits however this may have been due to 
pancreatic burnout.  Her exam and presentation were unconcerning 
for infectious etiology or a surgical abdomen. She is followed 
as an outpatient by Dr. ___.
.
Her pain was controlled initially with 3mg IV dilaudid Q3H.  Her 
TPN was stopped and she was made NPO. She received ___ mg IV 
Zofran Q6-8H for nausea.  Her diet was advanced to sips on HD2 
and she was transitioned to PO pain medication when tolerating 
sips.  Her TPN was restarted on HD3 and her home pain medication 
and nausea medications were resumed. At the time of discharge 
she was tolerating clears, on TPN, and tolerating PO pain and 
nausea medication. 
.  
# Pancytopenia - patient's baseline hct appears to be in the mid 
___ and her platelets in the low 100s.  The etiology of her 
pancytopenia is unclear. Previous iron studies showed lower 
ferritin but otherwise unremarkable labs and as such iron 
deficiency is an unlikely cause.  Her compazine and phenergen 
were discontinued for the majority of this hospitalization as 
these could have been offending agents for myelosupression; 
however, her blood counts did not improve upon withholding these 
medications and they were restarted due to refractory nausea. 
.
# GERD- continue PPI 40mg BID, this was not an active issue 
during this hospitalization
.  
# Depression- continue home regimen of sertraline, bupropion, 
trazadone.  This was not an active issue during this 
hospitalization
.

.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

It was a pleasure taking care of you at ___. You were admitted 
to the general medical floor after presenting with nausea, 
vomitting, and abdominal pain for 3 to 4 days. Your laboratory 
results including labs reflecting the possibility of infection 
(WBC) as well as your pancreatic enzymes (lipase, amylase) were 
normal. However, given your history of multiple episodes of 
chronic pancreatitis and your presenting symptoms, it was 
determined that this was a likely flare. Your diet was held for 
the first two days and you were treated with IV dilaudid and IV 
Zofran and Reglan.  Compazine and Fenergen were avoided since 
they may have caused low blood counts, however your blood counts 
did not improve without these medications and they were resumed. 
You should follow up with a hemotologist fo further evaluate 
these low blood counts. Your diet was advanced to sips and 
clears on day 3 of your stay and you were transitioned to oral 
pain and nausea medications. Your TPN was restarted. You should 
resume your usual medications upon returning home and should 
minimize use of dilaudid to the extent possible.

No changes were made to your medications. 

Please follow-up at the appointments below.
